extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and PTAB litigators (petitioners, patent owners, and counsel appearing before the PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and discretionary frameworks the PTAB applies when deciding whether to institute an inter partes review (analysis under 35 U.S.C. §§ 314 and 325(d), Advanced Bionics/Becton Dickinson, and Fintiv). Useful for evaluating whether to file or defend an IPR petition and for briefing remand/Director-review issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 314 "reasonable likelihood" standard for institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution of an inter partes review is authorized by statute when 'the information presented in the petition . . . and any response . . . shows that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the petition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. § 314 and 37 C.F.R. § 42.4. This is the statutory threshold the Board uses to determine whether to institute on the merits (separate from the Board's discretionary authorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution is discretionary under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although § 314 authorizes institution when the statutory standard is met, the Director and the Board retain discretion whether to institute review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities: Cuozzo Speed Techs., LLC v. Lee; SAS Inst. Inc. v. Iancu; Harmonic Inc. v. Avid Tech. The Board may deny petitions even if the statutory threshold is arguably satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 325(d) two-part Advanced Bionics framework
rubrics_metrics.description: When the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments were previously presented to the Office, the Board applies a two-part framework: (1) whether the same or substantially the same art or arguments previously were presented to the Office; and (2) if so, whether the petitioner has demonstrated that the Office erred in a manner material to the patentability of the challenged claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If part one is not satisfied, § 325(d) does not justify discretionary denial. If part one is satisfied, the Board then considers whether the petitioner has shown a material error by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becton, Dickinson factor (a): similarities/material differences between asserted art and prior art considered during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) the similarities and material differences between the asserted art and the prior art involved during examination;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor (a) helps decide whether the same or substantially the same art/arguments were previously presented during prosecution; assess how close the asserted references/combination are to what the Examiner saw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becton, Dickinson factor (b): cumulative nature of asserted art vs prosecution art
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) the cumulative nature of the asserted art and the prior art evaluated during examination;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether asserted references add only cumulative teachings relative to what the Examiner considered—if cumulative, weighs toward discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becton, Dickinson factor (c): extent to which asserted art was evaluated during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) the extent to which the asserted art was evaluated during examination, including whether the prior art was the basis for rejection;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Examiner actually evaluated and relied upon the asserted art during prosecution (e.g., used it as a rejection basis), that supports discretionary denial under § 325(d); absence of substantive consideration weighs against denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becton, Dickinson factor (d): overlap between prosecution arguments and petitioner's reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) the extent of the overlap between the arguments made during examination and the manner in which Petitioner relies on the prior art or Patent Owner distinguishes the prior art;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the prosecution record arguments to the petition's arguments—substantial overlap supports discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becton, Dickinson factor (e): whether petitioner pointed out Examiner error
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) whether Petitioner has pointed out sufficiently how the Examiner erred in its evaluation of the asserted prior art;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner must point to specific, material Examiner errors to overcome a § 325(d)-based discretionary denial. Generalized claims of failure are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becton, Dickinson factor (f): extent to which additional evidence warrants reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: (f) the extent to which additional evidence and facts presented in the Petition warrant reconsideration of the prior art or arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor (f) permits consideration of new or additional evidence (e.g., expert declarations, previously unconsidered portions of references, the sheer volume of an IDS) that might justify revisiting earlier prosecution decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Bionics — part two specific requirement (focus on Becton factors (c),(e),(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to part two of Advanced Bionics, 'a petitioner must explain, with reference to Becton Dickinson factors (c), (e), and (f), how the Examiner erred in overlooking the prior art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when asserted prior art was on an IDS, a petitioner must provide analysis showing the Examiner materially erred (or rely on additional evidence under factor (f)). Generalized statements of petition strength are not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS presentation can satisfy Advanced Bionics part one
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Challenging the claims using the same prior art that was previously presented on an IDS is sufficient to satisfy the first part of the Advanced Bionics framework.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the same references were provided in an Information Disclosure Statement during prosecution, that typically satisfies the 'previously presented' prong, but it does not end the § 325(d) inquiry—petitioner still must address part two.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as substantive consideration by Examiner (MPEP § 609.04(b) initialing vs substantive analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Examiner's initials on IDS pages may indicate the references were 'considered' under MPEP § 609.04(b), but initials on a lengthy, massive IDS do not by themselves show substantive consideration of particular references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will look for evidence that the Examiner substantively evaluated the reference (e.g., cited it as a basis for rejection or discussed its teachings), not merely that the reference appeared on an IDS or was initialed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard (37 C.F.R. § 42.100(b); Phillips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are construed 'in accordance with the ordinary and customary meaning of such claim as understood by one of ordinary skill in the art and the prosecution history pertaining to the patent.' Only those claim terms in controversy need to be construed, and only to the extent necessary to resolve the controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Phillips v. AWH. If the record does not present claim term disputes, the Board may adopt plain-and-ordinary meaning and proceed without express construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/analysis of level of ordinary skill in the art (POSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board preliminarily adopts a proposed POSA definition where supported by the record; here, a POSA would have 'a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, chemistry, physics, or an equivalent field, as well as 3–4 years industry experience, or a master's degree and 1–2 years industry experience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific findings regarding skill level are not required when the prior art itself reflects the appropriate level; cite Okajima v. Bourdeau and Litton Indus. Prods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 1 — stay likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the court granted a stay or evidence exists that one may be granted if a proceeding is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stay of parallel litigation reduces concern about inefficiency and strongly weighs against exercising discretion to deny institution. In ITC proceedings stays are unlikely, so this factor often favors denial when the ITC is advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 2 — proximity of trial date to Board deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Proximity of the court's trial (or final determination) date to the Board's projected statutory deadline for a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the parallel forum's final determination is before the Board's deadline (especially by several months), this weighs in favor of discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 3 — investment in parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment in the parallel proceeding by the court and the parties (how far advanced is the other forum?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant investments (completed discovery, completed claim construction, evidentiary hearings, post-hearing briefing) in the parallel proceeding support discretionary denial to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 4 — overlap of issues between proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlap between issues raised in the petition and in the parallel proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive overlap (same references/grounds and claims) weighs in favor of denial because the parallel proceeding will largely resolve the same disputes; limited overlap (many claims or grounds unique to the IPR) reduces the weight of this factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 5 — identity of parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner and the defendant in the parallel proceeding are the same party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the parties are the same across forums, this tends to favor discretionary denial (efficiency concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor 6 — other circumstances including merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Other circumstances that impact the Board's exercise of discretion, including the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may consider particular strengths or weaknesses of the merits, but 'compelling merits alone is not dispositive.' The Board applies a holistic assessment of all Fintiv factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic balancing of Fintiv factors for discretionary denial
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board takes 'a holistic view of whether efficiency and integrity of the system are best served by denying or instituting review' when evaluating Fintiv factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors 1–6 are balanced together (some may weigh for denial, some against). The Board makes a case-specific, discretionary determination based on the totality of circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: What petitioners must do when asserted art was on an IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if asserted prior art appeared on an IDS (satisfying part one), a petitioner 'must provide an analysis even when the asserted prior art is on an IDS, but the Examiner did not apply the reference.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should (a) point out specific Examiner errors (factor (e)); (b) show how the Examiner failed to evaluate the references (factor (c)); or (c) present additional evidence/facts (factor (f)) such as expert declarations or evidence that references were buried in a massive IDS so as to warrant reconsideration.
